items.body: Register Login Sabres To Activate Sam Carrick By Brennan McClain | at October 29, 2026 4:30 pm According to a team announcement , the Buffalo Sabres are expected to activate forward Sam Carrick from the injured reserve ahead of tonight’s contest against the Anaheim Ducks. Unfortunately, the Sabres also announced that forward Konsta Helenius will not finish the road trip with the club due to an upper-body injury. Carrick, 34, has not played since Buffalo’s October 15th matchup against the Toronto Maple Leafs due to a mid-body injury. The fourth-line forward went scoreless in four games before the injury with a -3 rating and averaged 7:34 of ice time per game. Still, much of Carrick’s value comes on the defensive side of the puck. He has averaged a 91.8% on-ice SV% at even strength throughout his career. Still, the Sabres will miss Helenius at least through the next two games. The Sabres announced that Helenius has already returned to Buffalo for further evaluation. Their current road trip through the Pacific Division will end this Saturday, and the Sabres don’t have a home game until November 4th. If they place Helenius on injured reserve retroactive to his most recent game, he would be eligible to return next Wednesday against the Ottawa Senators. In the second year of his entry-level contract, the former first-round pick has struggled offensively this season. Helenius has registered one goal and three points in 11 games with a -2 rating before suffering the upper-body ailment.

items.title: Flames awaiting update on injured goaltender Devin Cooley
items.body: Calgary Flames goaltender Devin Cooley remains under evaluation after suffering a lower-body injury during Wednesday's 4-0 loss in Edmonton. The 29-year-old was injured in a collision with Oilers forward Colton Dach in the crease with 12 seconds remaining in the first period. He stopped eight of nine shots before leaving the game and was replaced by Dustin Wolf. Flames head coach Ryan Huska said Thursday there was no further update on Cooley's condition. No timetable for his return has been announced. Cooley had started all four games of Calgary's recent four-game winning streak, which ended Wednesday. He posted a 1.50 goals-against average and .955 save percentage during that stretch.

By Josh Cybulski | at October 29, 2026 3:10 pm Pittsburgh Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas took a page from the Tampa Bay Rays’ playbook by signing forward Ville Koivunen to an eight-year, $32MM extension this past summer . As the Rays have done for years, Dubas locked up an unproven player with a big extension at a surprising price. It’s worked for the Rays for decades, but the NHL rarely does it, and Dubas could pioneer it with Koivunen. However, if it doesn’t work, Dubas will have a pricey gamble on his hands. But if it does, will it change how other GMs operate? It will be a long time before we know whether his deal will give Pittsburgh value, and two weeks ago it looked like a disaster. Kindel has two points and two assists in nine games this season for Pittsburgh and has not played since Oct. 19. items.body: Register Login Snapshots: Shabanov, Lardis, 2027 Draft By Ethan Hetu | at October 29, 2026 2:33 pm While it’s still very early in the 2026-27 season, it’s not too early to begin looking at players who may be setting themselves up to earn a big pay raise in the summer. With the salary cap rising at a steep rate, promising individual performances can have even more weight as teams look to identify and pay players before those players can realize the full extent of their value on the open market. The Anaheim Ducks’ decision to pay Tristan Luneau , with less than 30 NHL games to his name, a $7.2MM AAV on a long-term contract extension serves as an illustration of this principle in action. One player who is lining himself up to earn a substantial pay raise is Minnesota Wild winger Max Shabanov . The 26-year-old former KHL star endured a difficult NHL rookie season with the New York Islanders in 2025-26, and New York ultimately non-tendered him after he scored just 18 points in 44 games. The Wild inked Shabanov to a one-year, $1.6MM deal, and he’ll be an RFA with arbitration rights over the summer. His early-season form suggests a major pay raise could be in store, as he’s found himself a regular role on Minnesota’s top power play unit and has produced nine points in his first 13 games with the Wild.

items.summary: Most NHL fans accept the Edmonton Oilers and Vegas Golden Knights as by far the top two teams in the Pacific Division, but after one month of the season, is there a clear third?
items.body: Robert Edwards-Imagn Images Robert Edwards-Imagn Images Who Is Truly The Third-Best Team In The NHL's Pacific Division? Ryan Lambert Partner Oct 29, 2026 6:58 PM Published Oct 29, 2026 6:58 PM Most NHL fans accept the Edmonton Oilers and Vegas Golden Knights as by far the top two teams in the Pacific Division, but after one month of the season, is there a clear third? items.title: Dylan Larkin to stay out of games until Red Wings complete trade
items.body: The Detroit Red Wings ' former captain will not play until a trade occurs, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Thursday. The development follows head coach Todd McLellan's announcement that Larkin will not play against the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. McLellan said Detroit's interim general manager Shawn Horcoff would address the situation. Larkin, 30, requested a trade during the summer. He did report to the team, but was stripped of his captaincy. The three-time all-star, who has a no-trade clause, has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams. Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press has reported that Larkin's list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. While former general manager Steve Yzerman fielded calls for Larkin, those talks stalled while the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations once he was removed from his post on July 15. That search is ongoing but Horcoff was elevated to interim general manager in September and seemingly has the authority to complete a Larkin trade. One team notably not on Larkin's trade list is the Montreal Canadiens, even after Canadiens fans chanted "we want Larkin!" during a recent visit by the Red Wings. However, Red Wings assistant GM Kris Draper has watched the Canadiens live several times this season.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Lightning are getting one of their top players back into their lineup, and his arrival could not be coming at a better time. Veteran and franchise legend defenseman Victor Hedman will be back on the ice for the Bolts as they take on the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. Winger Brandon Hagel, who has not missed a game but had his status for this contest up in the air, will also play. The six-foot-seven No. 2 overall pick from the 2009 NHL Draft, Hedman has 4 points in 10 games this year while skating to a plus-5 rating on an average of 13:35 of time on ice per game. With J.J. Moser, Ryan McDonagh, John Carlson and Erik Cernak in the fold, the Lightning have been able to shelter Hedman and effectively manage his role in his age-35 season. With Hagel and Hedman both in the lineup, head coach Jon Cooper will deploy what has been a favorite strategy of his in running a lineup consisting of 11 forwards and 7 defensemen. Veteran forward Zemgus Girgensons will not play and is out on a day-to-day basis, and Tampa has plenty of depth defensively to spread minutes around on the back end. The Lightning, perennially one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, have looked like such to start this season, but a dearth of games played compared to their Atlantic Division foes has them sitting in sixth in the division by points, though they’re second by points percentage. Despite the overall strong start, Tampa has dropped its past two games as the Jets come to town, so the Bolts will be looking to get right against a Winnipeg team that started the year out hot but has lost six straight games to plummet down the Central Division standings.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Pittsburgh Penguins forward Ben Kindel is set to return to game action on Thursday against the the Utah Mammoth less than a week after suffering a medical episode on a team flight. Coach Dan Muse confirmed to reporters on Thursday morning that Kindel, as well as forwards Evgeni Malkin and Egor Chinakhov, are all expected to draw back in. Kindel collapsed on the team’s flight from Salt Lake City International Airport last week shortly after Pittsburgh’s previous outing against the Mammoth. According to Penguins GM Kyle Dubas, Kindel regained consciousness after receiving oxygen on the plane, having suffered a bout of vasovagal. The Mayo Clinic describes this as an event that causes “heart rate and blood pressure to drop suddenly” when the “body overreacts to certain triggers.” “Just really grateful for the Penguins staff, doctors, trainers, everybody who are so good, as well as the flight crew,” Kindel told reporters about the experience on Tuesday. “Just so really grateful for that, and they handled it with really good professionalism, and everything worked out good, so now I’m just looking to move forward.” Kindel said he returned to the ice last weekend after returning home to Pittsburgh, and used the extra time away from game action to get himself physically back up to speed. “Obviously, a couple weird days, but it feels normal now just being back with the guys,” Kindel added. “So yeah, just excited for the rest of the year.” Kindel is in his second season of NHL action, registering two goals and two assists through nine games. items.title: Injured Panthers Brad Marchand, Aleksander Barkov resume skating
items.summary: The Florida Panthers could be about a month away from nearing full forward health.
items.body: The Florida Panthers could be about a month away from nearing full forward health. Captain Aleksander Barkov and veteran winger Brad Marchand both resumed skating Thursday as they take a step toward a return from injury, head coach Paul Maurice told reporters . Barkov remains four weeks away from playing games while Marchand is three weeks out, Maurice added. The captain, who missed all of last season due to a right knee injury, went down in just his second game this season with a left knee injury that ultimately did not require surgery. His original timeline of six to eight weeks from the early October exit appears to still be intact. Marchand has also been out since early October with a left leg injury. “We’re no stranger to guys going down the last few years, and guys have done a great job of stepping up," Matthew Tkachuk said in the wake of the Marchand injury. “Worst case, you just got to win 1-0, 2-1.” Indeed, the Panthers have held their own without the star forwards, going 7-4-2 record in 13 games to hold the top wild-card spot in the East.

Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press has reported that Larkin's list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. items.body: Register Login Metro Notes: Garand, Flyers, Rangers Centers By Ethan Hetu | at October 29, 2026 8:34 am Though the New York Rangers’ competitive hopes for the 2026-27 season were dealt a massive blow when it was announced that star goaltender Igor Shesterkin would miss the rest of the season with an injury, the situation is not without its silver linings for the club. Shesterkin’s injury, along with a more minor injury suffered by veteran backup Joonas Korpisalo , has allowed goalie prospect Dylan Garand to have his longest stint in the NHL of his young career. So far, he’s generally impressed, even if he’s slowed down a bit as of late. Garand’s emergence could pay dividends for a Rangers team that traded away significant draft capital over the summer. According to The Athletic’s Vince Z. Mercogliano , the Rangers may try to capitalize on Garand’s increasing value next summer by trading him away, assuming Garand “puts together a solid season and teams come calling about a trade.” Mercogliano pointed out that New York’s situation with Garand is not entirely dissimilar to the situation they found themselves in back in 2015, when Cam Talbot emerged as a future No. 1 goalie while he was still Henrik Lundqvist’s backup. The Rangers ended up trading Talbot for a package of draft picks headlined by a second and third-rounder.

items.title: NHL Power Players returns for eighth season
items.summary:
Another hockey season means another season of NHL Power Players.
The League’s youth advisory board is returning again this season for its eighth year, bringing together 27 young hockey fans aged between 13-17 years old to help advise the League on hockey-related topics important to their generation.
items.body: Youth board made up of 27 teens to help advise League on hockey-related topics Another hockey season means another season of NHL Power Players. The League’s youth advisory board is returning again this season for its eighth year, bringing together 27 young hockey fans aged between 13-17 years old to help advise the League on hockey-related topics important to their generation. “I think hockey is often misunderstood among my generation,” said Madison Xu, a 17-year-old member of the advisory board from Vancouver. “Spreading the sport is something I care about, and I think the way it helped me, it can help other people as well.” The advisory board meets virtually two to three times per month to give these young fans an opportunity to offer feedback and suggestions to the League. Some Power Players even get to travel to different marquee events throughout the season. Xu described hockey as a “consistent presence in my life,” and said she’s been watching the sport with her dad over the last few years. “That’s something that brings me a lot of comfort and something I greatly value,” she said. She enters her first year with the Power Players and is looking forward to putting her best ideas forward throughout the season. “I really want to be contributing very thoughtfully to all the meetings that we’re having,” Xu said. “And give the most valuable insights that I can.” During the program, the Power Players can advocate for certain passion projects to help them gain traction within the League. Kade McKeever, a 17-year-old from Virginia in his second year with the program, used his time last year to make a presentation on adaptive hockey. items.title: EBUGs Unmasked: Inside the life of an emergency backup goalie
items.summary: It’s a full-time travelling job under the new NHL CBA. How does it work day to day?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Photo courtesy of Washington Capitals Just get any piece of his body to touch this puck, and Connor Leslie will be proud. He’s supposed to be embarking on a career in law enforcement right about now. He’s been paying the bills working at a gun range. Instead, he’s staring down Alex Ovechkin’s one-timer, again and again and again, until ‘Ovi,’ the greatest goal scorer who ever lived, feels like he has it calibrated well enough for the day. Leslie has to avoid fanboying out too much. He has a job to do. He’s trying to keep Washington Capitals goaltenders Logan Thompson and Charlie Lindgren fresh. It’s scary facing the patented Ovechkin shot, which beats Leslie most of the time – it’s famous for a reason, he says – but he’s thrilled if he can block, deflect, even graze one of them. Day to day, he’s doing his best to stand in for an NHL goalie, getting in front of shots, trying not to make things too easy for the Capitals’ players. He thinks he’s merely part of the background, barely noticed. But not today, when Tom Wilson asks the coaching staff to pause the drill instruction for an announcement. Leslie is turning 25 today, and he stands on the ice, in full NHL-regulation gear, listening to the Capitals sing Happy Birthday to him. It’s surreal. Leslie is one of them now. items.body: Company named League's official shipping and logistics partner NEW YORK – DHL and the National Hockey League (NHL) today announced a new multiyear international partnership, naming DHL an Official Shipping and Logistics Partner of the NHL with marketing rights in key European markets. The partnership provides DHL with an array of European marketing rights that will connect the brand with the NHL and its fans across Europe. Fans will see the DHL brand on the NHL’s digitally enhanced dasherboards and on virtual slot in-ice ads during European NHL game broadcasts. DHL will have the ability to include NHL Players in marketing campaigns to engage European NHL fans and receive prominent line of sight signage and branding during NHL Global Series games and for World Cup of Hockey 2028 games in Prague. DHL will also provide marketing support for the NHL's new prime time Monday Night Hockey broadcasts, providing passionate European hockey fans the ability to watch their favorite teams, and some of the NHL’s biggest stars, in prime time during the week. Utilizing the NHL’s vast marketing, digital, and social media channels, DHL will create co-branded campaigns, which include NHL.com international websites and country specific NHL social media channels throughout Europe. Content that showcases how DHL supports the NHL’s international logistics needs will be highlighted across NHL and DHL platforms and a Delivering Memories program delivering memorabilia to fans through a sweepstakes will be created. Across Europe, DHL will interact with fans at future Hockey Day in Germany, Sweden, Finland, and Czechia events, with unique activations at the NHL Global Series Fan Fest in Düsseldorf and other NHL Fan Fests in European cities throughout the year. items.summary: Sergei Bobrovsky is a quiet presence. But doubts swirling around him are getting louder.
items.body: But those observing the Toronto Maple Leafs from afar aren’t so sure. Not after Sergei Bobrovksy allowed three goals on the Calgary Flames first 12 shots Monday and helped the club dig a hole it couldn’t crawl out from. Not after the NHL’s oldest No. 1 goaltender allowed five more on just 17 Seattle Kraken shots Wednesday. What was supposed to be a bounce-back start resulted in his worst performance as a Leaf (.706 save percentage). And not after you realize the future Hall of Famer with the $7 million AAV has allowed three or more goals in nine of his 10 starts and has only won three of them (3-5-2). But unlike after Bobrovsky’s questionable performance in Alberta, the goaltender took more ownership. “I thought guys played well. You know, we deserved a point at least. It was good game. Only one of the Capitals’ goals didn’t feature a point from a member of the first line. items.body: Calgary Flames goaltender Devin Cooley was replaced by Dustin Wolf after the first period following a hard bump from Edmonton Oilers forward Colton Dach. Dach crashed into Cooley with 12 seconds remaining in the opening 20 minutes and received a two-minute penalty for goaltender interference. Cooley remained in for the final 12 seconds but was not on the bench to start the second. He was then ruled out for the remainder of the game with a lower-body injury, the team announced. The injury interrupted Cooley's run of hot play. The 29-year-old had allowed just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four games entering play Wednesday, good for a .955 save percentage. Cooley had allowed one goal on nine shots through 20 minutes against the Oilers. However, it isn't just Cooley's strong performance that's turned heads lately. items.body: Connor McDavid is red-hot to start the season, and the records are starting to pile up. With an assist in the first period against the Calgary Flames on Wednesday, the Edmonton Oilers captain set an NHL record for the longest season-opening assist streak. McDavid now has at least one assist in each of Edmonton's first 13 games this season, which breaks the previous record of 12 season-opening games held by Wayne Gretzky (1982-83), Ken Linseman (1985-86) and Sebastian Aho (2018-19). Wednesday's apple brought McDavid's point total to a ridiculous 35 points (12 goals, 27 assists) in just 13 games. I’m being honest with you. “Right now I’m focused on our team. … Quinn’s situation will resolve itself at some point in time, and like I said, this does not keep me awake at night. items.body: Register Login Capitals Activate Logan Thompson; Reassign Mitch Gibson By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 3:58 pm After returning as a regular to practice yesterday, the Washington Capitals will return their starting netminder to the active roster. According to beat reporter Sammi Silber , the Capitals activated netminder Logan Thompson from the injured reserve and assigned Mitch Gibson to the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Thompson has been on Washington’s injured reserve with a lower-body ailment since their October 20th matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Fortunately, the Capitals had only one game in the past week, limiting Thompson’s absence. Despite beating the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday, Washington likely wasn’t confident in Charlie Lindgren as the starter moving forward. The Capitals’ defense bailed him out for much of the game, limiting the Sabres to 21 shots on net through 63:42. Still, Lindgren stopped only 15 of those attempts, leading to a disappointing .857 SV% on the night. Now the Capitals can return to a netminder who has been on cruise control since joining the organization ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. This season, Thompson has earned a 4-3-0 record in seven starts with a .901 SV% and 2.90 GAA, including 1.9 Goals Saved Above Average. Throughout the past two years, Thompson has managed a dominant 62-27-12 record with a .911 SV% and 2.46 GAA, including two fourth-place finishes in Vezina Trophy voting. Meanwhile, Gibson returns to AHL Hershey without debuting in the NHL. He’s gotten off to a subpar start this season, splitting his first two appearances with an .881 SV% and 3.50 GAA.

items.body: “I’m sure there’ll be an opportunity at some point where we’re going to play together, and I’m sure it’ll be a lot of fun.” — Auston Matthews on Gavin McKenna , September 16 SEATTLE — It took until Game 15, but Gavin McKenna finally walked into the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ dressing room and saw his name to the left of Auston Matthews’ on the top line, along with Jack Roslovic. “When you see that, I think a little bit of a boost of confidence,” McKenna said Wednesday morning at Climate Pledge Arena, ahead of the Leafs’ game against the Seattle Kraken. “When you’re playing with two guys like that, you've got to make sure you're working. I want to make the most out of this opportunity, so I’m looking forward to it.” So is Leafs Nation, a fan base begging to see what magic Toronto’s two most recent first-overall draft picks can conjure in regular rotation. “Whenever he’s open, you want to find him in a spot because he's dangerous in all areas of the ice. So, you want to get him the puck,” McKenna said of his new centreman. But remember, it was mentor Matthews who set up McKenna’s first-ever NHL goal three weeks ago, in an emotional comeback win over Nashville. “His playmaking is something. I didn’t really know how good he was at making those plays coming into the league. I think he's made a ton of nice plays not a lot of guys can make. So, when he’s got the puck on his stick, you've got to be ready as well,” McKenna noted. McKenna and Matthews sit beside each other on the road and have flashed power-play chemistry. Blockbuster trades that cause seismic shifts across the landscape of the NHL don't happen often, let alone in the first month of the season. items.summary: In Oliver Moore’s 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago’s offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal.
items.body: CHICAGO — In Oliver Moore 's 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago's offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal. In Moore's 71st game, he was all over the ice in a big win for the Blackhawks. That's how it's going at the moment in Chicago, where the team's youngest players are still learning on the job. Moore was a healthy scratch for Sunday’s 3-2 loss to Florida, but he returned to the lineup Tuesday night and played quite well in a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings. “I didn’t expect anything less,” coach Jeff Blashill said. “He actually was playing good hockey. I felt it was a moment where him and our team needed to make sure we learn these lessons about not beating ourselves. But he’s played good hockey, so it’s not like he went through a stretch where he hadn’t been playing well. He stepped right back in and did a good job.” Moore, a first-round pick in the 2023 draft, is a key figure for Chicago as it tries to find the other side of years of rebuilding. The 21-year-old Minnesota native signed a $21.25 million, five-year contract in September. Losers of eight of their first 12 games, the Blackhawks are looking for more offence once again. They are averaging 2.17 goals, ranking No. 31 in the NHL going into Wednesday's action. They averaged just 2.56 goals last season. Moore has elite speed and athleticism, but he is still working on finishing his scoring opportunities. He has two goals and one assist in 11 games after he had five goals and 14 assists in 51 games all of last season. Facing Montreal on Friday, he tried to make a backhand pass from the corner to Ryan Greene in the middle. It was intercepted by Owen Beck, who started a rush that led to Jake Evans' tying score in the first period of the Canadiens' 4-1 win.

items.summary: Here’s Eric Engels with the latest on the Dylan Larkin-to-Montreal buzz. It’s not about to die down, with the Red Wings heavily scouting the Canadiens, who have the assets to get this trade done.
items.body: The price for Detroit’s Dylan Larkin, according to league sources, isn’t just exorbitant. “It should be,” said one Eastern Conference executive, granted anonymity to speak openly about another team’s business. “He’s been a No. 1 centre for almost all his time there, and that has its own price. But factor in his cap hit ($8.7M through 2031) in this landscape, and that’s worth a premium.” This conversation was playing out over text while the Canadiens were completing a win in Chicago under the watchful eyes of Red Wings assistant general manager Kris Draper, who’s surely been following them for no other reason than due diligence for a potential trade. He was there in Toronto for Game 1 between the Canadiens and Leafs, then in Montreal for Canadiens-Sharks Oct. 20, and once again in Chicago for Canadiens-Blackhawks last Friday. There were rumblings he was at the Heritage Classic in Winnipeg Sunday—though we didn’t see him there—but he was definitely at Enterprise Center for Canadiens-Blues Tuesday, and it’s not because he’s suddenly become a fan of either team. If all of this smacks as absurd to you because Larkin hasn’t officially listed Montreal as one of the cities he’s willing to waive his no-movement clause for, consider that there aren’t many—if any—teams on his list loaded with the type of assets the Canadiens have to offer for the player’s services. Still, that doesn’t mean they’re willing to meet the current price that’s been set for the 30-year-old’s services. “It’s not about to come down, either, with the Wings hanging around and winning games,” added our league executive, and he was right. After losing five of their first six—one in a shootout to Montreal and one in overtime to the New Jersey Devils—the Wings have won four of six for a respectable 5-4-3 record.

items.title: Where the NHL salary cap could soar to in the next three years
items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap is still going through a “smoothing” process as the league comes out of the pandemic-induced flat cap wanting to avoid a sudden jump. But as we get to the end of that process, how high could the upper limit climb? Frank Seravalli has the story.
items.body: At the very end of his Board of Governors’ media conference last month on the 101 st floor of 30 Hudson Yards in Manhattan, NHL commissioner Gary Bettman offered an unprompted forewarning on the future of hockey’s salary cap. “Somebody had asked about the cap going up,” Bettman jumped in. “Please keep in mind that the cap going up at the rate it’s going up, it’s still a function of recapturing where we’re supposed to be after years of a flat cap,” Bettman said. “That number continues to be [managed] as we try to create a smooth increase in cap and not drive everyone crazy by who happened to be a free agent in a year with a huge jump.” Bettman reminded that once the system recaptures it, which he estimated “it will take two more years give or take,” then the cap “will go up at the same rate as revenues grow.” Fortunately for Bettman and the NHL, revenue continues to climb at record rates. But that means the salary cap will require even more finessing to smooth out drastic increases – because the cap is being kept so artificially low this season that there is a pending explosion. According to projections run by Sportsnet , verified by multiple team, league and Players’ Association sources, the NHL’s salary cap ceiling could reach $150 million USD by 2029-30 – just three seasons from now. That is a whopping 44 per cent increase from this season’s ceiling of $104 million. The calculation is relatively simple and we can use crumbs of information from Bettman’s media availability. He said last month that this season’s projected revenue was “just north” of $8 billion, or $8 billion “and change” in “mixed currency” since the league’s teams earn revenue in American and Canadian dollars. items.title: Charlie Jacobs to take over from father as Bruins’ governor

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images A huge change in operations in New England. On Wednesday, the Boston Bruins announced that CEO Charlie Jacobs is going to take over as the team’s governor from his father, Jeremy M. Jacobs, who held the role for 51 years. Charlie will represent the club on the NHL’s Board of Governors. “It is a tremendous honor to step into the role as governor of the Boston Bruins,” the younger Jacobs said in a release. “Representing the team that has been part of my family for the past 51 years. I step into this role with the goal of continuing to build upon the incredible legacy and the impact that my dad has had on this franchise and the NHL over his five decades of leadership. Dad will continue to serve as my mentor and sounding board through this next era of the Bruins. I am looking forward to partnering with the NHL Board of Governors Chairman Ted Leonsis, Vice Chair Murray Edwards, our peers, and Commissioner Bettman on continuing to grow this beautiful game that we all love.” The move to promote Charlie comes as Jeremy is starting to move out of the spotlight. Last month, he stepped down as Chairman of the league’s board of governors, and Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis was unanimously voted in as the new chair. Charlie has been part of the organization since 2000, when he was named the Bruins’ alternate governor. He also serves as the CEO of Delaware North, a multinational food service and hospitality company, which has ownership shares of NESN, the Bruins’ local broadcaster.

items.body: In the midst of a prolonged losing streak, the Vancouver Canucks were in desperate need of some good vibes. With just one win in the month of October, it was getting understandably difficult for the Canucks to maintain some positivity about what they're building towards. And when Quinn Hughes and the Minnesota Wild handed the Canucks their 10th straight loss Sunday, morale was at an all-time low. But Tuesday night against the Anaheim Ducks, the Canucks clawed back from an early deficit, earning an impressive 6-5 victory to get finally back into the win column thanks to an overtime snipe from Filip Hronek and some late-game heroics from Jonathan Lekkerimaki. It was a win that took a fair bit of resilience from a dejected Vancouver squad. For much of the night in Southern California, the Canucks looked to be headed to a familiar fate. A three-goal second period from the Ducks put the Canucks into a 4-1 hole that seemed, at times, insurmountable. But goals from Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak in the early goings of the third cut into the Ducks' lead, perfectly setting the stage for Lekkerimaki to score twice with the net empty to force overtime. It was the sixth time in franchise history that the Canucks rallied from a three-goal, third-period deficit. Ottawa's Ridly Greig had a short-handed breakaway opportunity, but Hill raced out of his net to the right circle to poke away the puck. Vegas quickly got the puck to the other end, and Bowman deposited a rebound off Ivan Barbashev's shot from the right circle with 11 seconds left in the period. Ottawa answered just 34 seconds into the third when Drake Batherson made a terrific pass to Pinto in the slot for the tying goal. That was Batherson's eighth point in five games, and it's the sixth game in a row the Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal. Lavoie, playing in his 27th game, then put Vegas back on top with his goal after a pass from Ville Heinola.

items.title: Fowler cementing place as Canadiens starter with another win
items.summary: After a 46-save shutout against the Blues, goaltender Jacob Fowler is making it impossible for the Canadiens to turn away from him, writes Eric Engels.
items.body: Jacob Fowler pushed to his right, stopped a shot from Jake Neighbours, and then quickly scrambled to his left and sprawled to take a sure goal away from Dylan Holloway. It was his last save of the night, a 10-beller if we’ve ever seen one, and we’re not even sure it was the best of the 46 he made to preserve a 2-0 shutout for the Montreal Canadiens over the St. Louis Blues. We can’t say how this game might have turned out with Jakub Dobes in Montreal’s net. In St. Louis, a city in which Dobes spent his teenage years as a USHLer, he might’ve been just as brilliant. But Martin St. Louis elected not to start Dobes and had to be elated he instead stuck with the hot hand — and not just after watching Fowler stuff Holloway on the doorstep of his crease with 1:12 remaining in a game the 21-year-old had already dominated. Fowler was the story of Sunday’s Heritage Classic; the big-game goalie shining on the biggest and brightest stage , taking yet another giant leap on his rapid ascent up the NHL ladder and cementing his place as Montreal’s starter. He made 33 saves on 34 Winnipeg Jets shots for his fifth straight win just two nights after stopping 20 of 21 against the Chicago Blackhawks for his fourth. On Monday, Fowler was named the league’s third star of the week for those performances. items.title: Hellebuyck impresses in first start with Devils: 'He was exceptional'
items.summary: DALLAS -- Connor Hellebuyck’s tenure with the New Jersey Devils began on a high note.
items.body: Goalie allows just one goal in win against red-hot Stars, was 'making plays everywhere' DALLAS -- Connor Hellebuyck ’s tenure with the New Jersey Devils began on a high note. The 33-year-old goaltender made 17 saves for his new team in a 5-1 victory against the Dallas Stars at American Airlines Center on Tuesday. The start came less than a week since the three-time Vezina Trophy winner was acquired by New Jersey in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets on Friday for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to forward Alexander Command , a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft. When asked what was going through his head during the national anthem, Hellebuyck answered with a single word: “Finally.” It makes sense, considering the trade for Hellebuyck came on the day his suspension, which began on Sept. 16, was scheduled to come to an end. As a result of the impasse with Winnipeg, Tuesday was also his season debut. Not that you would have known it by watching Hellebuyck play. “If you asked me, I was ready two months ago,” he said. “I just had the mindset since the day I got here that I want to get in.” And he made an impact right away, according to Devils captain Nico Hischier . “He came in and was making plays everywhere,” Hischier said. “He just spread this calmness out.
